metadata.case_name: SIN FU YAU v. CHEUNG KWOK LEUNG KEITH AND OTHERS

injuries.description: fracture at the base proximal phalanx of left 1st toe and crack at the base of the distal phalanx.
source: fracture at the base proximal phalanx of left 1st toe and crack at the base of the distal phalanx.

injuries.description: superficial abrasions, swelling, bruises and tenderness over the left 1st metatarsal area
source: superficial abrasions, swelling, bruises and tenderness over the left 1st metatarsal area
injuries.icd_description: Multiple superficial injuries of ankle or foot

injuries.description: decreased range of movement over the left 1st metatarsal phalangeal joint
source: decreased range of movement over the left 1st metatarsal phalangeal joint
injuries.icd_description: Other specified injuries to the ankle or foot

manifestations.description: tenderness around the 1st proximal interphalangeal joint with limited big toe motion
squeezing the 1st metatarsal head of the left big toe caused pain
left big toe movement was impaired
dorsal flexion and plantar flexion power of the left ankle was slightly limited by pain
extension power of the left big toe was mildly weaker
pain of the dorsum of the 1st metatarsal after walking for 30 minutes
pain on lateral left ankle and left hip after walking for 30 minutes
decrease in climbing speed and tolerance due to left foot pain
lifting tolerance to be 30 pounds, carrying tolerance was 23 pounds, tolerance of repetitive crouching was 30 minutes
mildly reduced left ankle muscle power
superficial abrasions, swelling, bruises and tenderness over the left 1st metatarsal area

treatments_received: first aid at first aid station
treatment at Tuen Mun Hospital Accident and Emergency Clinic

losses.description: left big toe suffering from pain and stiffness; impaired left big toe movement of 7% (equivalent to 3% whole person impairment)
inability to climb scaffolding; decrease in climbing speed and tolerance due to left foot pain; lifting tolerance 30 pounds, carrying tolerance 23 pounds, tolerance of repetitive crouching 30 minutes
